Jonas — quick technical note, sorry for the terse reply, hammering through a sprint but wanted to get specifics on record.

Short answers up front:
- Selective routing: supported. Our smart routing can pin requests to a UK-resident dedicated pool or a regional hosted instance based on a policy header. We can implement a per-route enforcement that drops into UK-region instances for "residency=true" calls.
- KV/prefix caching: we keep the KV cache local to the serving pool; if requests are pinned to UK nodes, cache never leaves those hosts. For multi-variant fallbacks (e.g., if UK pool is full) we'd need a fallback policy — we can default to queued retry or degrade to a compatible lower-tier model in-region.
- Audit logs + evidentiary artifacts: we produce per-request trace IDs, token counts, latency + node-id, and an access log that can be exported. For TIA scoping you will need our subprocessor map, TLS/Ciphering details, and a sample of the request-level audit log (redacted). We can produce an "evidence packet" containing: subprocessor list, proc map, retention policy excerpt, KV locality statement, and a sample redacted trace (CSV).

Limitations/notes:
- Redaction: we do not perform semantic redaction server-side by default. If the customer requires content redaction before any non-UK processing, we'd need to add a redaction step (edge pre-processor) or require client-side redaction. That increases latency and may change cost profiles.
- Cold failover: routing to a remote fallback is allowed but will create cross-border transfers unless you set the policy to block or queue.

I've attached the proxy diagram Jon sent with arrows labelled for the routing decisions — happy to iterate. If Laura confirms the legal path (IDTA vs SCC-only), we can draft the evidence matrix and timeline.

Kim

Summary (short):
- Feasibility: Yes — Redwood supports a selective onshore proxying pattern. We can pin requests to UK-resident serving pools and ensure KV/prefix caches remain local to UK hosts.
- Cross-border risk & IDTA: Proxying to UK-only hosts will reduce cross-border exposure for routed requests.
